deadlocks.explanation: Session 75 held shop.customers and wanted shop.orders; session 73 held shop.orders and wanted shop.customers. With the same order in both, the second would simply wait instead of deadlocking.

fixes.detail: Make every code path that changes shop.customers and shop.orders do it in one order (for example, always the parent row first, and rows sorted by key). Then the second transaction waits instead of deadlocking.
fixes.title: Touch tables and rows in the same order everywhere

fixes.detail: Do reads, validation and outside calls before the transaction starts; hold locks only for the writes.
fixes.title: Keep transactions short

fixes.detail: A deadlock victim can be retried safely; the application should catch error 1205 and run the transaction again.
fixes.title: Retry the victim

deadlocks.headline: Two transactions locked shop.customers and shop.orders in opposite order and waited on each other; session 75's transaction was rolled back.

processes.statement: BEGIN TRAN; UPDATE shop.customers SET created_at = DATEADD(second, 1, created_at) WHERE id = 2; WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:01'; UPDATE shop.orders SET total = total + 1 WHERE id = 2; ROLLBACK;

BEGIN TRAN; UPDATE shop.orders SET total = total + 1 WHERE id = 2; WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:01'; UPDATE shop.customers SET created_at = DATEADD(second, 1, created_at) WHERE id = 2; WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:01'; ROLLBACK;

deadlocks.explanation: The read finds rows through ix_customers_email and then looks each one up in the table's main index; the write changes the main index first and then ix_customers_email. Each ends up holding the lock the other needs next. It recurs whenever the two statements touch the same rows at the same time.

fixes.detail: Add the columns the read needs to ix_customers_email (as INCLUDE columns) so it never touches the main index the write locks. The query's plan in Queries shows the Key Lookup and its output columns.
fixes.title: Make the read skip the lookup

fixes.detail: With READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT on, reads use row versions instead of shared locks, so a read can't be part of this cycle. It costs some tempdb space for the versions.
fixes.sql: ALTER DATABASE [culprit_demo] SET READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE;
fixes.title: Let reads stop taking shared locks

fixes.detail: A deadlock victim can be retried safely; the application should catch error 1205 and run the transaction again.
fixes.title: Retry the victim

deadlocks.headline: Key-lookup deadlock on shop.customers: a read through ix_customers_email and a write to the same rows took their locks in opposite order; session 61's transaction was rolled back.

processes.statement: SELECT id, name, segment FROM shop.customers WHERE email = @P1
UPDATE shop.customers SET email = @P1 WHERE id = @P2
